Financial due diligence

# Red flags in an Indian company’s financial statements

Before you invest in, acquire or sign up an Indian partner, read its accounts the way an Indian auditor would. Most warning signs are disclosed — in the auditor’s report, the notes and public records — if you know where to look.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·6 min read

Get the accounts reviewed
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- Start with the auditor's report and its CARO annexure — adverse answers point to what to investigate.
- Related parties, ageing schedules, MSME dues and contingent liabilities are the notes that matter most.
- Cross-check with MCA charges, EPFO payment history, court records and GST returns.

## Getting the accounts

Every Indian company files its audited financial statements with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (Form AOC-4). Anyone can buy copies of a company’s filed documents on the MCA portal for a small fee — no permission needed. Ask the company for the latest three years in full (including notes and the auditor’s report), and compare them with what was filed. See how to verify an Indian company.

## 13 red flags and where to find them

Red flag | Where to look | What it can mean | What to ask for | 
Qualified, adverse or disclaimer opinion; going-concern paragraph | Auditor’s report | The auditor could not agree with, or could not verify, part of the accounts | The basis for the modification and whether it has been fixed | 
Stock statements to banks don’t match the books | CARO 2020, clause 3(ii)(b) | Inventory or receivables overstated to one side — the bank or the accounts | The reconciliation sent to the bank | 
Statutory dues unpaid over six months | CARO, clause 3(vii) | Cash strain; interest and penalties building up | Current status of GST, TDS, PF and ESI payments | 
Income surrendered in a tax assessment but not in the books | CARO, clause 3(viii) | Unrecorded sales or cash dealings | The assessment order | 
Loan defaults, short-term money used for long-term assets, wilful-defaulter tag | CARO, clause 3(ix) | Liquidity stress or diversion of funds | Bank sanction letters and repayment history | 
Fraud reported or whistle-blower complaints | CARO, clause 3(xi) | Control failures | What happened and what changed | 
Cash losses or auditor resignation | CARO, clauses 3(xvii)–(xviii) | Business or governance trouble | The outgoing auditor’s reasons | 
Large sales, purchases or loans with promoter-linked firms | Related-party note | Profit can be shifted in or out of the company | Pricing basis and board/shareholder approvals | 
Receivables over a year old or marked disputed | Receivables ageing schedule | Revenue that may never be collected | Customer-wise ageing and collections after year-end | 
Overdue dues to micro and small suppliers | MSME note | Interest at three times the bank rate; tax disallowance of late payments | Supplier-wise list and payment dates | 
Big tax demands or guarantees for group companies | Contingent liabilities | Liabilities that are not in the balance sheet yet | Orders, appeals and guarantee deeds | 
Profit mostly from “other income” | Statement of profit and loss | The core business may be loss-making | Breakdown of other income | 
Late or missing filings; frequent auditor changes | MCA records | Weak compliance culture | Reasons and any penalties paid | 

## The auditor’s CARO report

Under the Companies (Auditor’s Report) Order, 2020 (CARO), auditors of most companies must answer about 21 specific questions — on inventory, loans, statutory dues, defaults, fraud, related parties, cash losses and more. Read it line by line: an adverse answer is a direct pointer to what to investigate. CARO does not apply to one-person companies, small companies, and private companies below set limits (paid-up capital and reserves up to ₹1 crore, borrowings up to ₹1 crore and revenue up to ₹10 crore) — so for small targets, you need to do more of this work yourself.

## The notes that matter most

- Related parties: list every transaction with the promoter family’s other businesses. In Indian family groups this is normal — the question is whether pricing is fair and approvals were taken. See partnering with family businesses.

- Ageing schedules: since April 2021, Schedule III requires ageing of receivables, payables and capital work-in-progress. Old balances are where problems hide.

- MSME dues: companies must disclose overdue amounts owed to micro and small suppliers under the MSMED Act. Late payments attract interest at three times the RBI bank rate, and income-tax law disallows the expense if payment is late.

- Contingent liabilities: tax and GST demands under appeal, bank guarantees and corporate guarantees given for group companies.

## Cross-checks against public records

- Charges on MCA: secured loans registered against the company’s assets should line up with borrowings in the balance sheet.

- EPFO establishment search: provident-fund payment history gives a rough check on headcount and payroll.

- Court records (eCourts): recovery suits, cheque-bounce cases and insolvency petitions.

- GST returns: with the company’s consent, compare turnover in GST returns with revenue in the accounts.

An illustrative report format: sample India due diligence report. The full list of checks: due diligence checklist.

## How we help

We read Indian accounts for foreign investors, acquirers and buyers — and report in plain English with the questions to put to the company. Financial due diligence in India · partner due diligence.

## Sources

- Companies (Auditor's Report) Order, 2020 — Ministry of Corporate Affairs
- MSMED Act, 2006 — Ministry of MSME
- EPFO — establishment search
- eCourts services
See also: credit rating and default checks.
See also: forensic audit & fraud investigation in India.

## Frequently asked questions
What are the red flags in an Indian company's financial statements?
Common ones are a qualified or adverse audit opinion, adverse answers in the auditor's CARO report (unpaid statutory dues, loan defaults, fraud, cash losses), large related-party transactions, old or disputed receivables, overdue MSME dues, big contingent liabilities and late MCA filings.

Where can I get an Indian company's financial statements?
Companies file audited financial statements with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs in Form AOC-4. Copies can be bought on the MCA portal for a small fee, without the company's permission.

What is CARO 2020?
The Companies (Auditor's Report) Order, 2020 requires auditors of most Indian companies to report on specific matters such as inventory, loans, statutory dues, defaults, fraud and related parties. It does not apply to one-person companies, small companies and private companies below set size limits.

Why do MSME dues matter in due diligence?
Overdue amounts to micro and small suppliers carry interest at three times the RBI bank rate under the MSMED Act, and late payments can be disallowed as an expense for income tax — both can hit profits and cash.

Compliance calendar

# Tax & compliance calendar: November–December 2026

The busiest stretch of the Indian compliance year: transfer-pricing reports, two ITR deadlines, annual company filings, the December advance-tax instalment and three 31 December deadlines. Every date, in order.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·5 min read

Get your filings done
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- Form 3CEB is due 31 Oct; ITR for audit cases 21 Nov; transfer-pricing cases 30 Nov.
- Advance tax third instalment: 15 Dec (75%).
- 31 Dec: belated ITR, GSTR-9/9C and the FAST-DS foreign-asset window.

Date | What’s due | Who | 
29–30 Oct | AOC-4 original due date (30 days from a 30 September AGM) — additional fees waived until 31 December 2026 (MCA General Circular 05/2026) | Companies | 
30 Oct | LLP Form 8 (statement of account and solvency) | LLPs | 
31 Oct | Form 3CEB transfer-pricing report — not covered by the CBDT extension | Companies with international transactions | 
31 Oct | TDS and TCS returns for July–September | Deductors and collectors | 
7 Nov | TDS / TCS deposit for October | Deductors | 
11 Nov | GSTR-1 for October | Monthly GST filers | 
15 Nov | PF / ESI for October; TDS certificates for July–September | Employers; deductors | 
20 Nov | GSTR-3B for October | Monthly GST filers | 
21 Nov | Income-tax return for audit cases (CBDT Circular 7/2026) | Companies, audited businesses, partners of audited firms | 
29 Nov | MGT-7 original due date (60 days from a 30 September AGM) — additional fees waived until 31 January 2027 | Companies | 
30 Nov | Income-tax return for transfer-pricing cases | Companies with Form 3CEB | 
30 Nov | Liaison office annual statement — Form 162 (formerly 49C) for the year to 31 March 2026 under the earlier rules | Foreign companies with an Indian liaison office | 
2–4 Dec | RBI Monetary Policy Committee meeting | Borrowers, NRIs, investors | 
7 Dec | TDS / TCS deposit for November | Deductors | 
11 Dec | GSTR-1 for November | Monthly GST filers | 
15 Dec | Advance tax — third instalment (75% cumulative) | Companies, businesses, individuals with tax over ₹10,000 | 
20 Dec | GSTR-3B for November | Monthly GST filers | 
31 Dec | Belated income-tax return for 2025-26 | Anyone who missed the due date | 
31 Dec | GSTR-9 / GSTR-9C annual returns for 2025-26 | GST taxpayers (GSTR-9 optional up to ₹2 crore; 9C above ₹5 crore) | 
31 Dec | FAST-DS 2026 — last date to declare foreign assets; no extension per the official FAQ | Residents and former residents with undisclosed foreign assets | 

## Watch-outs

- Transfer-pricing cases were not extended: Form 3CEB is due 31 October and the ITR 30 November. See Form 3CEB due date.

- MCA relief (24 October): AOC-4 can be filed without additional fees until 31 December 2026 and MGT-7/MGT-7A until 31 January 2027. Miss those dates and fees run from the original due date. AGM deadlines and ADT-1 are not extended — details.

- FAST-DS closes on 31 December — see the FAST-DS guide.

- GST: the 57th Council’s reforms still need notifications or law changes — status.

Earlier dates: October–November 2026 calendar · ITR details: ITR due dates 2026.

## Sources

- CBDT Circular 7/2026 (income-tax department)
- FAST-DS FAQs (income-tax department)
- Taxscan — GSTR-9/9C enabled for FY 2025-26
- TaxGuru — ICSI seeks MCA filing extension

## Frequently asked questions
What is the ITR due date for audit cases in 2026?
21 November 2026 for companies, audited businesses and partners of audited firms, under CBDT Circular 7/2026. Transfer-pricing cases were not covered and remain due on 30 November 2026.

When is the third advance tax instalment due?
15 December 2026 — 75% of the year's estimated tax, cumulatively.

What is the last date for GSTR-9 and GSTR-9C for FY 2025-26?
31 December 2026. GSTR-9 is optional for turnover up to ₹2 crore; GSTR-9C applies above ₹5 crore.

Has the AOC-4 / MGT-7 due date been extended for 2026?
Yes. MCA General Circular 05/2026 (24 October 2026) allows AOC-4 to be filed without additional fees until 31 December 2026 and MGT-7/MGT-7A until 31 January 2027 for FY 2025-26. Filing after those dates attracts fees from the original due date; AGM deadlines are not extended.

Please note: this guide is general information based on the rules as they stood on the review date above. Regulations and RBI/CBDT procedures change often — please get advice on your specific facts before acting.

Glossary

# India business glossary for foreign companies — 44 terms in plain English

The acronyms you’ll meet when dealing with an Indian company, investing or setting up in India — each in one line, with a link to the full guide.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 22 October 2026·8 min read

Ask about a term
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Company identifiers 8Tax 10GST and trade 7Foreign investment (FEMA) 12Deals and disputes 7

## Company identifiers
CINCorporate Identity Number — the unique number the Ministry of Corporate Affairs gives every Indian company. More.LLPINLLP Identification Number — the equivalent of a CIN for a limited liability partnership.DINDirector Identification Number — a unique number every director of an Indian company must hold. More.MCA / MCA21The Ministry of Corporate Affairs and its online portal, where company records, filings and financial statements are kept. More.ROCRegistrar of Companies — the MCA office that registers companies and receives their filings.AOC-4 / MGT-7Annual company filings with MCA: AOC-4 for financial statements, MGT-7 for the annual return (shareholders, directors). More.Private limited companyIndia's most common company form, with limited liability and restrictions on share transfers — the usual vehicle for foreign subsidiaries. More.LLPLimited liability partnership — open to foreign investment only in sectors allowing 100% automatic-route FDI without conditions. More.

## Tax
PANPermanent Account Number — the income-tax identifier for people and entities, including foreign companies with Indian tax matters. More.TANTax Deduction Account Number — needed by those who deduct tax at source (individual buyers of property from NRIs can use PAN since October 2026). More.TDSTax deducted at source — tax the payer withholds from payments such as salaries, fees, royalties and payments to non-residents. More.TCSTax collected at source — collected by the seller or bank on certain transactions, such as overseas remittances under LRS. More.Income-tax Act, 2025The law that replaced the Income-tax Act, 1961 from 1 April 2026, renumbering sections and forms. More.Form 41The treaty-relief information form a non-resident files online — formerly Form 10F. More.TRCTax residency certificate — issued by a person's home tax authority; needed to claim treaty rates in India. More.DTAADouble taxation avoidance agreement — India's tax treaty with another country. More.PEPermanent establishment — a taxable presence of a foreign company in India, such as an office or dependent agent. More.Forms 145 / 146The remittance declaration (145) and CA certificate (146) for payments abroad — formerly Forms 15CA and 15CB. More.

## GST and trade
GST / GSTINGoods and Services Tax — India's indirect tax; GSTIN is the 15-character registration number. More.IGSTIntegrated GST — charged on inter-state supplies and imports.LUTLetter of Undertaking — lets an exporter export goods or services without paying IGST. More.OIDAROnline information and database access or retrieval services — the GST category for foreign digital services sold into India. More.IECImport Export Code — the DGFT registration most businesses need to import or export. More.DGFTDirectorate General of Foreign Trade — the government body for trade policy and IEC registration.SEZSpecial Economic Zone — designated zones with export-focused tax and customs treatment.

## Foreign investment (FEMA)
FEMAForeign Exchange Management Act, 1999 — the law governing foreign investment and cross-border payments. More.FDIForeign direct investment — investment by a non-resident in an Indian company's capital. More.Automatic routeFDI that needs no prior government approval, only reporting — available in most sectors. More.Press Note 3The 2020 rule requiring government approval for investment from countries bordering India — eased in 2026 for non-controlling stakes up to 10%. More.FC-GPRThe RBI form reporting shares issued to a foreign investor — due within 30 days of allotment. More.FC-TRSThe RBI form reporting a share transfer between a resident and a non-resident — within 60 days. More.FLA returnAnnual return on foreign liabilities and assets filed with RBI by 15 July. More.FIRMSRBI's online portal for foreign-investment reporting.AD bankAuthorised dealer bank — a bank permitted by RBI to handle foreign-exchange transactions and many FEMA approvals.ODI / APROverseas direct investment by Indian residents, and the annual performance report filed on each overseas entity. More.ECBExternal commercial borrowing — loans to Indian entities from foreign lenders.Liaison / branch / project officeWays a foreign company can be present in India without an Indian company, each with RBI rules. More.

## Deals and disputes
NCLTNational Company Law Tribunal — handles insolvency, mergers and company-law disputes.IBCInsolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 — India's insolvency law.SEBISecurities and Exchange Board of India — the securities-market regulator.AIFAlternative Investment Fund — a SEBI-registered private fund (Categories I, II and III). More.GIFT City / IFSCIndia's international financial services centre in Gujarat, regulated by IFSCA. More.DPIITDepartment for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade — issues FDI policy and press notes.CCICompetition Commission of India — reviews larger mergers and acquisitions.

Please note: this guide is general information based on the rules as they stood on the review date above. Regulations and RBI/CBDT procedures change often — please get advice on your specific facts before acting.

- India–EU FTA signature (targeted December 2026).

## Frequently asked questions
What changed for foreign investors in India in 2026?
Among others: the Income-tax Act 2025 took effect on 1 April 2026; Press Note 2 (2026) eased rules for investors with up to 10% non-controlling land-border ownership; from June 2026 any individual abroad can buy listed Indian shares directly; insurance moved to 100% automatic-route FDI; and trade agreements with the UK and New Zealand took effect.

Is the India–EU trade agreement in force?
Not yet. Negotiations concluded on 27 January 2026 and signature is targeted for December 2026.

A fixed-scope verification of one Indian company from public records — registrations, filed accounts, charges, directors and payment details — with an optional site visit and a short English report.

How is it different from due diligence?
It answers whether a company is real, solvent-looking and roughly what it claims. Full due diligence adds a deep financial, tax and FEMA review, management meetings and deal recommendations.

On this page

- What it covers
- Optional site visit
- When you need more
- FAQ

Questions answered

# Due diligence in India: 16 questions answered

The questions foreign companies ask before checking an Indian partner, supplier or target — answered in a sentence or two, current to October 2026.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 22 October 2026·6 min read

Ask your question
hello@durgeshchavda.com

About these answers: written by CA Durgesh Chavda, Chartered Accountant (ICAI), from the practice’s own guides. General information — ask us about your deal.
Basics 4Records and checks 4Scope, time and cost 3Rules that apply 5

## Basics

### What is due diligence on an Indian company?
An independent check of an Indian company before you invest in it, buy it or partner with it — its identity, finances, tax, regulatory standing, owners and premises. More.

### Can due diligence in India be done remotely?
Most of it can — public records, filed accounts, data rooms and management calls. A premises visit adds what records can't show; we do both from offices in Ahmedabad, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Rajkot and Dubai. More.

### Who does due diligence in India for foreign companies?
Chartered Accountants for financial, tax and FEMA work, alongside lawyers for legal diligence. CA Durgesh Chavda's team works for foreign companies and reports in English. More.

### What's the difference between verification and full due diligence?
Verification answers 'is this company real and roughly what it claims?' from records and a visit. Full due diligence reviews three years of financials, tax, FEMA, related parties and liabilities, with deal recommendations. More.

## Records and checks

### Are Indian private companies' accounts public?
Yes. Financial statements and annual returns are filed with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and can be viewed for about ₹100 per company. More.

### How do I check an Indian company's GST status?
Use 'Search Taxpayer' on the GST portal — it shows whether the GSTIN is active and whether returns are filed. More.

### Can I check the directors of an Indian company?
Yes — MCA records list directors and their other companies; integrity checks add regulatory lists, insolvency and court records, sanctions and media. More.

### What are the biggest red flags?
Filed revenue far below claims, cancelled GST, undisclosed charges, unpaid tax demands, related-party cash flows, promoters linked to struck-off companies, and payment requests to another entity. More.

## Scope, time and cost

### How long does due diligence in India take?
A verification with a site visit typically takes days to a couple of weeks; full financial, tax and FEMA due diligence depends on the company's size and how fast data arrives — the timetable is agreed at the start. More.

### What drives the cost of due diligence in India?
Scope (verification vs full diligence), the company's size and number of entities, data quality, site visits and travel, and deadlines. We fix the scope and fee upfront. More.

### What will I receive?
A written English report: what was checked, findings with references to records, red flags and a conclusion — plus agreement points for deals. More.

## Rules that apply

### Does India's anti-bribery law apply to foreign companies?
Yes — since July 2018 companies carrying on business in India can be liable for bribes by associates unless they had adequate procedures. More.

### Do US companies still need FCPA checks on Indian partners?
Yes — US enforcement priorities narrowed in 2025, but third-party due diligence remains central to a credible compliance programme. More.

### What do UK companies need?
Bribery Act 'adequate procedures' and, for large organisations, 'reasonable procedures' under the failure-to-prevent-fraud offence in force since 1 September 2025. More.

### What about EU and German supply-chain rules?
Germany's supply-chain due-diligence duties still apply (reporting suspended); the EU CSDDD applies from 26 July 2029 and the Forced Labour Regulation from 14 December 2027. More.

### What FEMA checks matter in a deal?
That every past foreign investment was reported (FC-GPR within 30 days, FC-TRS within 60 days) and priced at fair value — and that your own deal follows the same rules. More.
Unfamiliar term? See the India business glossary for foreign companies.
See also: due diligence cost.
Choosing an adviser? Big 4 or a smaller firm for due diligence in India.

# Partnering with an Indian business? We check them for you, on the ground.

Before you sign a joint venture, distribution, supply, licensing or outsourcing agreement with an Indian company, CA Durgesh Chavda’s team checks who they really are, how they really perform and what could go wrong — and reports to you in English.

## What we check, by type of partnership

Partnership | Your main risk | What we focus on | 

Joint venture | Partner’s past liabilities, control and exit | Full financial, tax and FEMA review; shareholding and charges; FDI route and pricing; exit-clause compliance — see the JV guide | 

Distributor / reseller | Credit risk, reputation, territory conflicts | Filed accounts, GST filing record, customers and receivables, litigation, other brands carried |

Investment or acquisition | Valuation and hidden liabilities | Full financial, tax and FEMA due diligence | 

## Three levels of checks

01
### Verify
Company records, GST and import–export registrations, filed financial statements, charges, director history and a premises visit. Answers “is this company real and roughly what it claims?”

02
### Review
Three years of financials, GST and income-tax position, related parties, customers and receivables, litigation through public records and counsel, and a management meeting.

03
### Diligence & structure
Full financial, tax and FEMA due diligence, red-flag report, deal-structure and tax advice, and drafting points for your agreement with your lawyers.

## Promoters and directors

In India, the people behind a company matter as much as the company. With your mandate we review promoters’ and directors’ other companies (including struck-off ones), public litigation records, regulatory actions and adverse media — and, for anti-bribery programmes, government links and how intermediaries are paid. Checks follow Indian data-protection law and are limited to what your decision needs.

## What you receive

- A written report in English: what we checked, what we found, red flags and a plain conclusion.

- Copies or references for every public record relied on.

- For deals: suggested conditions, warranties and protections for your agreement.

- Optional: a call with your legal, compliance or investment committee.

## How we work with you abroad

- Engagement letter and NDA by e-signature; scope and fee fixed upfront.

- Calls on your time zone — US, UK, Europe, Gulf, Singapore, Japan, Australia.

- Visits from our offices in Ahmedabad, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Rajkot and Dubai; other locations by arrangement.

- Legal opinions come from lawyers; we coordinate with your counsel in India or at home.

## Frequently asked questions
How do I do due diligence on an Indian company before partnering?
Start with free public records — MCA company data, GST registration and import-export code — then review its filed financial statements, tax position, charges, litigation and promoters, and visit the premises. For joint ventures or large contracts, commission a full financial, tax and FEMA review from an Indian CA.

Can someone in India check a business partner on our behalf?
Yes. CA Durgesh Chavda's team checks Indian partners for foreign companies — records, finances, tax, regulatory standing, promoters and premises — and reports in English, working remotely and on the ground.

What are the red flags in an Indian partner?
Filed revenue far below what is claimed, a struck-off or non-filing status, cancelled GST, undisclosed charges on assets, unpaid tax demands, related-party money flows, promoters linked to failed companies, and pressure to pay into a different entity's account.

Do you do background checks on Indian directors?
Yes, with your mandate and within Indian data-protection law: their other directorships, public litigation and regulatory records, and adverse media relevant to your decision.

# Due diligence in India for US companies

Sourcing from India, appointing a distributor, building a team or buying a company? We check the Indian side for US businesses — and write it up so your compliance, legal and deal teams can use it.

Key takeaways
- US FCPA enforcement narrowed in 2025, but third-party due diligence remains central to compliance.
- In India, check ownership, government links and how intermediaries are paid.
- The India–US trade deal's first tranche was reported finalised in Oct 2026 but isn't signed.

## Why companies from here use us

- US groups are shifting sourcing, engineering and back-office work to India — new partners need checking fast.

- Third parties — distributors, agents, customs brokers, consultants — are where anti-bribery risk sits.

- US deal teams want findings in their language: quality of earnings, liabilities, conditions to close.

## Your home-country rules — and what they mean for an Indian partner

- FCPA: after the February 2025 executive order paused enforcement, the DOJ’s June 2025 guidelines narrowed priorities to cases harming US interests — and in March 2026 the DOJ issued a department-wide corporate enforcement and self-disclosure policy. Fewer cases, sharper targets: intermediaries remain central, and risk-based third-party due diligence is still what a credible compliance programme shows.

- What that means in India: know who owns and controls your partner, whether any owners or agents are government officials, and how commissions and “facilitation” payments are made — then keep the evidence.

## The India side

- The first tranche of an India–US trade agreement was reported as finalised in October 2026 but is not yet signed — tariffs remain a moving target, so supplier contracts need flexibility.

- Indian subsidiaries and capability centres: subsidiary compliance and building teams in India.

- US parent with Indian operations: India–US tax treaty and repatriation.

- Promoters, directors, government links and how intermediaries are paid — for your anti-bribery and supply-chain files.

- Premises visits from Ahmedabad, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Rajkot or Dubai, with a written report in English.

- Full scope: partner due diligence · investment due diligence · supplier verification.

We are Chartered Accountants, not lawyers: home-country legal advice on compliance programmes stays with your counsel. Our reports are built to slot into their files.

Do US companies still need FCPA due diligence on Indian partners?
Yes. US enforcement priorities narrowed in 2025, but the FCPA remains in force, intermediaries remain the main risk, and risk-based third-party due diligence is still a core part of an effective compliance programme.

Can someone in India do due diligence on our Indian supplier?
Yes. We check Indian suppliers and partners for US companies — records, finances, tax, ownership, government links and premises — and report in English.

# Due diligence in India for UK companies

With the India–UK trade agreement in force, more UK firms are signing Indian suppliers, distributors and JV partners. We check them on the ground — and give your compliance file the evidence UK law now expects.

Key takeaways
- CETA has applied since 15 July 2026; UK firms are signing more Indian partners.
- Failure to prevent fraud (since 1 Sep 2025) and Bribery Act s.7 both reward documented partner due diligence.
- We check Indian partners on the ground and report in English.

## Why companies from here use us

- CETA has applied since 15 July 2026, cutting tariffs and opening services.

- UK corporate-offence regimes make your procedures for checking third parties a legal defence.

- One English-language report your legal, procurement and finance teams can all use.

Met an Indian partner at the UK’s CETA Marketplace in Mumbai (13 October 2026) or on a trade mission? Start with an India Company Check (USD 249) before you sign.

## Your home-country rules — and what they mean for an Indian partner

- Bribery Act 2010, section 7: a company is liable if an associated person bribes on its behalf, unless it had adequate procedures — proportionate due diligence on partners and intermediaries is one of them.

- Failure to prevent fraud (Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023), in force since 1 September 2025: applies to large organisations meeting two of — turnover over £36m, assets over £18m, more than 250 staff. The defence is having reasonable procedures, which the company must prove.

- Recent enforcement shows the risk often sits with JV partners and local “fixers”.

## The India side

- CETA and the Double Contributions Convention — see India–UK trade deal guide.

- Setting up in India: India for UK companies.

- Premises visits from Ahmedabad, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Rajkot or Dubai, with a written report in English.

## Frequently asked questions
Does the UK failure to prevent fraud offence apply to Indian partners?
It can: a large UK organisation can be liable for fraud by associated persons acting for it, including overseas partners, unless it had reasonable procedures — which include risk-based due diligence on those partners.

What are adequate procedures under the Bribery Act for India?
Proportionate, risk-based procedures including due diligence on Indian agents, distributors and JV partners — ownership, government links, payment arrangements and track record — plus contractual controls and monitoring.

When did the India–UK trade agreement take effect?
On 15 July 2026.

# Due diligence in India for German and EU companies

European buyers sourcing from India face more supply-chain rules than ever — and an India–EU trade agreement is on the way. We check Indian suppliers and partners on the ground and document it for your compliance files.

Discuss your Indian partner
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Talk it through first — free. Book a 15-minute intro call with Durgesh to scope your requirement, timeline and fee.Book a free 15-min intro
Key takeaways
- LkSG duties still apply; reporting is suspended and an amendment is pending.
- CSDDD applies from 26 July 2029 (Omnibus thresholds); the Forced Labour Regulation from 14 Dec 2027.
- CBAM's definitive phase began 1 Jan 2026 — Indian steel and aluminium suppliers need emissions data.

## Why companies from here use us

- The India–EU FTA was concluded in January 2026; signature is targeted for December 2026, with entry into force expected in 2027.

- EU supply-chain and carbon rules push requirements down to Indian suppliers.

- German Mittelstand firms need a reliable partner in India — not a large agency.

## Your home-country rules — and what they mean for an Indian partner

- Germany’s Supply Chain Act (LkSG): the due-diligence duties still apply; the reporting duty has been suspended in practice and an amendment is pending.

- EU CSDDD after the 2026 Omnibus (Directive (EU) 2026/470): applies to EU companies with 5,000+ employees and over €1.5bn turnover, and non-EU companies with over €1.5bn EU turnover — from 26 July 2029. Their suppliers will be asked for evidence well before then.

- EU Forced Labour Regulation: applies from 14 December 2027 — products made with forced labour can be banned from the EU market.

- CBAM: the definitive phase started on 1 January 2026. EU importers of Indian steel and aluminium need verified emissions data; without it, default values raise costs (small importers of 50 tonnes a year or less are exempt).

## The India side

- Setting up in India: Deutsch · Français · India for European companies · India–EU FTA guide.

- Swiss, Norwegian and Liechtenstein companies: the India–EFTA agreement has applied since 1 October 2025 — TEPA guide.

- Premises visits from Ahmedabad, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Rajkot or Dubai, with a written report in English.

## Frequently asked questions
Do German companies still need supply-chain due diligence on Indian suppliers?
Yes. Under Germany's Supply Chain Act the due-diligence duties continue even though the reporting obligation has been suspended in practice and an amendment is pending.

When does the EU CSDDD apply?
After the 2026 Omnibus amendments, from 26 July 2029, for EU companies with 5,000+ employees and over €1.5bn turnover, and non-EU companies with over €1.5bn turnover in the EU.

How does CBAM affect Indian steel and aluminium suppliers?
Since 1 January 2026 EU importers pay for embedded emissions; they need verified emissions data from Indian suppliers, otherwise higher default values apply.

JV guide

# Joint venture in India: a guide for foreign companies

A joint venture with an Indian company combines your product or capital with a partner’s market access. It also combines your fortunes — which is why the structure, the rules on pricing and exit, and the diligence on your partner matter so much.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·7 min read

Plan your JV
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- Most foreign JVs in India use a private limited company under the automatic FDI route.
- Shares must be priced at fair value; options are allowed but no assured return.
- Diligence on the Indian partner before the term sheet prevents most JV disputes.

## Choosing the JV vehicle

Vehicle | When it fits | Watch out for | 

Private limited company (most common) | Most JVs — clear shareholding, board control, ESOPs, raising capital | Company-law compliance; FDI rules on pricing and reporting | 

LLP | Service JVs with simple governance | Foreign investment only in sectors with 100% automatic-route FDI and no performance conditions | 

Contractual JV (no new entity) | Distribution, licensing, project cooperation | Permanent-establishment and withholding-tax exposure for the foreign party | 

## Foreign investment rules

- Route and caps: most sectors allow foreign investment under the automatic route; some have caps or need government approval. Check before agreeing the shareholding split.

- Land-border countries: if your group has beneficial owners in a country bordering India, non-controlling stakes up to 10% can use the automatic route since the 2026 amendment; above that, or with control, government approval is needed.

- Pricing: shares issued to the foreign partner must be priced at no less than fair value, supported by a valuation from a CA, merchant banker or cost accountant.

- Reporting: FC-GPR within 30 days of allotment; FC-TRS for any transfer between the partners; the annual FLA return. See the FC-GPR guide.

- Downstream investment: if the JV is owned or controlled by non-residents, its own investments in other Indian companies count as indirect foreign investment and follow the same rules.

## Exit, options and deadlock

- Put and call options are allowed for foreign investors, but with a minimum lock-in and exit at a price consistent with FEMA’s pricing rules — no assured return.

- Build in deadlock resolution, tag-along and drag-along rights, non-compete scope and what happens to IP and the brand on exit.

- Large JVs may need Competition Commission approval.

## Tax in brief

- The JV company can opt for a 22% base corporate rate (about 25.17% all-in).

- Dividends to the foreign partner: 20% plus surcharge and cess, or the treaty rate — see repatriating profits.

- Royalties, technical fees and services charged by the foreign partner must be at arm’s length (transfer pricing) and carry withholding.

## Diligence on your partner — before the term sheet

Most JV disputes trace back to something knowable at the start: liabilities in the partner’s existing business, related-party dealings, unreported foreign investment or promoters with a history. Use the partner due-diligence checklist, or have us run it: due diligence on an Indian business partner.

## Sources

- RBI — Master Directions (Foreign Investment in India)
- DPIIT — FDI policy
Most Indian partners are family-run: partnering with an Indian family business.

## Frequently asked questions
Can a foreign company form a joint venture in India?
Yes. Most sectors allow foreign investment in an Indian JV company under the automatic route, subject to sectoral caps, FEMA pricing rules and reporting such as FC-GPR within 30 days of allotting shares.

What is the best structure for a JV in India?
Usually a private limited company: clear shareholding, board control and the ability to raise capital. An LLP suits simple service JVs only where 100% FDI is allowed automatically without conditions.

Are put options allowed in Indian JVs with foreign partners?
Yes, with a minimum lock-in and an exit price consistent with FEMA pricing rules — the foreign partner cannot be guaranteed an assured return.

What due diligence should be done before a JV in India?
Financial, tax and FEMA review of the partner's existing business, its shareholding and charges, litigation, related parties and the promoters' track record — before signing a term sheet.

Please note: this guide is general information based on the rules as they stood on the review date above. Regulations and RBI/CBDT procedures change often — please get advice on your specific facts before acting.

AEO · AI search visibility

# AEO services — be the answer when buyers ask AI

Your next client may never see a list of links. They’ll ask ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity “who can help me with…” and act on the answer. We make sure that answer can include you — with the same method we used on this website.

Book an AEO call
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Talk it through first — free. Book a 15-minute intro call with Durgesh to scope your requirement, timeline and fee.Book a free 15-min intro

## What AEO is
Answer engine optimization (AEO) is the work of making your business the source AI assistants quote, cite or recommend when people ask questions in your field. Read the full explainer: What is AEO?
| SEO | AEO | 

Goal | Rank a link on a results page | Be the answer — quoted, cited or recommended by an AI assistant | 

Where | Google and Bing results | ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, Copilot, Grok, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, voice assistants | 

What wins | Relevance, links, technical health | Clear answers, trusted entity facts, structured data, citations to sources, mentions across the web — on top of good SEO | 

How it’s measured | Rankings, clicks | How often you’re named or cited for the questions your buyers ask | 

“GEO” (generative engine optimization) is used for much the same work. The terms overlap — what matters is that SEO stays the foundation and AEO builds on it.

## Why it matters for high-value B2B services

- Buyers ask, then shortlist. Founders, CFOs and investors increasingly ask an assistant for options before they search or ask for referrals.

- Answers name only a few firms. A results page shows ten links; an AI answer often names two or three providers. Being one of them is worth more than a page-two ranking.

- Accuracy is the moat. In finance, tax, legal and regulated sectors, assistants favour sources that are specific, current and consistent. That’s where a CA-led approach — fact-checked, sourced, dated — wins.

## What we do

Workstream | What it covers | 

1. AI visibility audit | We ask the major assistants the questions your buyers ask and record who gets named and cited; a technical and content audit explains why | 

2. Entity & trust signals | One consistent description of your firm across your site, profiles and directories; Organization / Person / Service structured data; disambiguation from similarly named firms | 

3. Crawl access | AI crawler rules, llms.txt and full-text files, sitemaps with accurate dates, IndexNow, Bing and Google webmaster setup | 

4. Answer-first content | Pages that answer real buyer questions in the first lines — quick-answer boxes, question-led headings, comparison tables, FAQs, cited sources and review dates | 

5. Service + place pages | Pages for each service in each market you serve, so “who does X in Y?” has an answer pointing to you | 

6. Off-site mentions | The profiles, directories, Q&A answers and articles AI systems learn from and cite — planned and drafted for you | 

7. Monitoring | A fixed set of buyer questions re-tested every month across assistants, plus Search Console and Bing data | 

## How engagements work

We implement the plan — technical setup, entity fixes, answer-first pages, structured data — on your site or with your developers.

A monthly retainer: new answer content, off-site mentions, monitoring and a short report on what moved.

## Where we work

AEO is done remotely, so location doesn’t limit us. We work with firms in India, the United States and Canada, the UK and Europe, the UAE and the Gulf, Singapore and the rest of Asia, Japan and Korea, Australia and New Zealand, Africa and Latin America.

- Multilingual answers: AI assistants answer in the buyer’s language. We test your buyers’ questions in English and in the languages of your markets, and structure pages so assistants can cite them — this site has pages in Japanese, German, French, Korean and Spanish.

- Local search engines and assistants: beyond ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Perplexity, we check Copilot and Bing (which many assistants draw on) and, where relevant, regional assistants.

## What we don’t promise

No one can guarantee that an AI assistant will name you — answers are generated, change over time and differ by user. We promise the work, the measurement and honest reporting. Agencies that guarantee “#1 in ChatGPT” are guessing.

## Frequently asked questions
What are AEO services?
Answer engine optimization services make a business more likely to be quoted, cited or recommended by AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot and Google AI Overviews — through technical access, consistent entity information, answer-first content, structured data, off-site mentions and monthly monitoring.

What is the difference between AEO and SEO?
SEO aims to rank a link on a results page; AEO aims to have your content used in the answer an AI assistant gives. AEO builds on SEO — a site that search engines can't crawl or trust rarely appears in AI answers.

How long does AEO take to show results?
Technical and on-page changes can be picked up by search-connected assistants within weeks; changes in what models 'know' without searching take longer, because they depend on retraining. Expect to measure progress monthly over at least three months.

Can you guarantee my business will appear in ChatGPT?
No. AI answers are generated and vary by user and over time, so no honest provider can guarantee placement. We commit to the work and to measuring it transparently.

Do you work with businesses outside finance?
Yes, mainly B2B and professional-services businesses where accuracy and trust drive buying decisions.

Do you offer AEO services outside India?
Yes. AEO work is done remotely for firms in the US, Canada, the UK and Europe, the UAE and Gulf, Singapore and Asia, Japan and Korea, Australia and New Zealand, Africa and Latin America — including testing buyers' questions in their own languages.

AEO guide

# What is AEO? Answer engine optimization, explained

Search is turning into conversation. When someone asks an AI assistant a question, it answers — and names a few sources. AEO is how you become one of them.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·7 min read

Talk about AEO
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- AEO makes your business the source AI assistants quote, cite or recommend.
- It builds on SEO: crawlable, clear, specific, current and consistent content wins.
- Measure it by testing your buyers' questions across assistants every month.

## AEO in one paragraph

Answer engine optimization (AEO) is the practice of making your content and your business the source that AI assistants and AI search features quote, cite or recommend. It targets ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, Copilot, Grok, Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode, and voice assistants.

| SEO | AEO | 

Goal | Rank a link on a results page | Be the answer — quoted, cited or recommended by an AI assistant | 

Where | Google and Bing results | ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, Copilot, Grok, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, voice assistants | 

What wins | Relevance, links, technical health | Clear answers, trusted entity facts, structured data, citations to sources, mentions across the web — on top of good SEO | 

How it’s measured | Rankings, clicks | How often you’re named or cited for the questions your buyers ask | 

“GEO” (generative engine optimization) is used for much the same work. The terms overlap — what matters is that SEO stays the foundation and AEO builds on it.

## How answer engines choose what to say

- Search-connected answers pull pages from a search index at the time of the question — Google’s for Gemini and AI Overviews, Bing’s for ChatGPT search and Copilot, and other indexes for other assistants — then summarise and cite them.

- Built-in knowledge comes from what the model learned in training, drawn from the public web: websites, profiles, directories, forums and news. That’s why consistent mentions across the web matter.

- Both reward the same things: pages that are crawlable, clear, specific, current and consistent with what the rest of the web says about you.

- Academic work on “generative engine optimization” found that adding citations to sources, quotations and statistics made content noticeably more visible in AI-generated answers.

## A 12-point AEO checklist

- AI crawlers (and Bingbot and Googlebot) are allowed in robots.txt.

- The site is verified in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools, with a sitemap that has accurate last-modified dates.

- New and updated pages are pushed to search engines quickly (IndexNow, indexing requests).

- An llms.txt summary — and ideally a full-text version — tells AI systems what you do.

- One consistent description of your business everywhere: website, LinkedIn, directories, Google Business Profile.

- Organization, Person, Service, FAQ and article structured data, with profiles linked via sameAs.

- Every key page answers its main question in the first two or three lines.

- Headings phrased as the questions buyers actually ask.

- Specifics: numbers, dates, rules, comparisons — not generic marketing copy.

- Sources cited and a visible “last reviewed” date.

- Pages for each service in each market you serve.

- A monthly test: ask the main assistants your buyers’ questions and record whether you’re named.

Score yourself with the AEO readiness checker.

## Common mistakes

- Treating AEO as a replacement for SEO — it’s built on top of it.

- Blocking AI crawlers by accident (often through a security plugin or CDN setting).

- Different business descriptions on different profiles, which makes assistants unsure who you are.

- Believing anyone who guarantees placement in AI answers.

Want it done for you? AEO services · see the method on this site: AEO case study.

## Sources

- Wikipedia — Generative engine optimization
- Aggarwal et al. — GEO: Generative Engine Optimization (arXiv)
- Contently — What is answer engine optimization (Feb 2026)
New research: AI Visibility Index 2026 — how 96 B2B websites score for AI readiness.
Related: AEO for accounting & CPA firms · AEO for fintech · AEO for SaaS.

## Frequently asked questions
What is AEO in marketing?
Answer engine optimization — optimising content and business information so AI assistants and AI search features (ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot, Google AI Overviews) quote, cite or recommend you when people ask questions.

Is AEO the same as GEO?
They overlap heavily. GEO (generative engine optimization) is often used for being cited in generative AI answers; AEO is often used more broadly for answer-style results including featured snippets and voice. In practice the same work serves both.

Does AEO replace SEO?
No. AI assistants rely on search indexes and on what the web says about you, so SEO remains the foundation; AEO adds answer-first content, entity consistency and AI-specific access.

How do you measure AEO?
By testing a fixed set of buyer questions across assistants each month and recording whether you're named or cited, alongside Search Console and Bing data for the pages those answers draw on.

Case study

# AEO case study: what we did on our own website

Before offering AEO to clients, we ran it on ourselves. Here is exactly what we changed on durgeshchavda.com from late September 2026, and what the data shows so far — including what we can’t prove yet.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·5 min read

Get an AEO audit
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- Daily Google impressions rose about five-fold in under four weeks (≈200 to ≈1,030 a day).
- New pages were indexed within one to two days; the site ranks first on Bing for its founder's name.
- AI citations are tracked by monthly manual tests — the data so far is early.

## The numbers (Google Search Console)

Period | Google impressions | Per day | 

First 9 days of tracking (to 6 Oct 2026) | 1,800 | ≈ 200 | 

7 days to 9 Oct 2026 | 2,500 | ≈ 360 | 

7 days to mid-October 2026 | 4,610 | ≈ 660 | 

7 days to 21 October 2026 | 7,240 (104 clicks) | ≈ 1,030 | 

- The site appeared for 194 different search queries in its first 9 days of tracking, and for 693 in the latest 28 days.

- Page-one positions for niche terms such as the 57th GST Council meeting, Form 5472 due dates and FC-GPR deadlines.

- New pages indexed by Google within one to two days of publishing; 142 pages indexed by 22 October 2026.

- Page-one rankings within days for new topics, such as “Form 41 India” (positions 1–11) and “NRI tax consultants in Ahmedabad” (position 3).

- First on Bing for the founder’s name and its variants.

## What we did

- Crawl access: AI crawlers welcomed in robots.txt; llms.txt and a full-text llms-full.txt; sitemap with real last-modified dates; IndexNow on every release; RSS feed.

- Entity: one consistent description, Person and Organization structured data, a disambiguating description and an about page with quotable key facts.

- Answer-first pages: quick-answer boxes, key takeaways, question-led headings and FAQs on every important page.

- Sources and dates: every guide cites its sources and shows a review date; rules are fact-checked before publishing.

- Coverage: service + place pages (Dubai, Ahmedabad, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Gurgaon, Hyderabad, Gujarat) and pages for the questions foreign companies and NRIs actually ask.

- Freshness: trending rules and deadlines covered within days, with accurate dates.

- Internal links: exact-phrase links from related pages to each target page.

## What we can’t prove yet

- Search Console doesn’t separate AI Overview appearances, and assistants don’t publish citation data — so AI citations are tracked by monthly manual tests, which began in October 2026.

- Three weeks is short. Some of the growth is a new site being discovered; we’ll update this page with longer-term data.

Want the same for your business? AEO services · check your AEO readiness.

## Sources

- Google Search Console (site's own data, Oct 2026)

## Frequently asked questions
Does AEO work for professional-services firms?
On this website — a Chartered Accountant's practice — answer-first pages, entity consistency, crawl access and fast indexing coincided with daily Google impressions rising about five-fold in under four weeks. AI citations are measured separately through monthly tests.

What was the most effective AEO change?
Coverage and clarity together: pages that answer specific buyer questions in their first lines, with cited sources and current dates, published and indexed quickly.

Questions answered

# India for NRIs and foreigners: 36 questions answered

The questions NRIs, foreign investors and foreign companies ask most — each answered in a sentence or two, current to October 2026, with a link to the full guide.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·9 min read

Ask your question
hello@durgeshchavda.com

About these answers: written and reviewed by CA Durgesh Chavda, Chartered Accountant (ICAI), and updated as Indian rules change. They are general information — for your situation, ask us.
For NRIs: tax 6For NRIs: money and property 6For foreign individuals 4For foreign companies: entering India 6For foreign companies: tax and money 6Checking and buying Indian companies 4Trade deals 4

## For NRIs: tax

### Do NRIs have to pay tax in India?
Yes, on Indian income only — rent, NRO interest, dividends and capital gains on Indian assets. Income earned and received abroad isn't taxed in India. Read more.

### What are the NRI tax slabs for 2026-27?
The same as residents under the new regime (nil to ₹4 lakh, then 5% to 30%), but without the rebate that makes ₹12 lakh tax-free for residents. Read more.

### Is NRE interest taxable?
No. NRE and FCNR interest is tax-free for NRIs; NRO interest is taxable. Read more.

### Do NRIs need to file an Indian tax return?
Yes if Indian income is above the basic exemption — and usually worth it to recover excess TDS. Read more.

### How many days in India make an NRI resident?
Generally 182 days in a year. For Indian citizens and people of Indian origin visiting India, the shorter test applies only if Indian income exceeds ₹15 lakh — 120 days plus 365 days over the previous four years. Read more.

### What is FAST-DS 2026?
A one-time window until 31 December 2026 to declare undisclosed foreign assets (60% cost up to ₹1 crore) or assets missed in Schedule FA (₹1 lakh up to ₹5 crore). Read more.

## For NRIs: money and property

### How much can an NRI repatriate from India?
Up to USD 1 million per financial year from NRO accounts after tax, with Forms 145 and 146; NRE balances are fully repatriable. Read more.

### Does the US 1% remittance tax apply to bank transfers to India?
No — only to transfers funded with cash, money orders or cashier's checks, from 1 January 2026. Read more.

### How much TDS applies when an NRI sells property?
TDS at non-resident capital-gains rates — buyers often deduct on the full price, far more than the final tax; a lower-deduction certificate (Form 128) fixes that. Read more.

### Does a buyer need a TAN to buy property from an NRI?
Not since 1 October 2026 for resident individual and HUF buyers — they can deposit TDS using their PAN through Form 141. Read more.

### Can NRIs buy agricultural land?
No. NRIs and OCIs can buy homes and commercial property but can only inherit agricultural land, plantations or farmhouses. Read more.

### Can NRIs apply for IPOs in India?
Yes — through ASBA from an NRE or NRO account, holding shares in an NRI demat account; check each offer document. Read more.

## For foreign individuals

### Can a foreigner buy property in India?
A foreign national living outside India who isn't an OCI can only inherit Indian property or lease it for up to 5 years. Read more.

### Can foreigners invest in Indian shares?
Yes. Since 12 June 2026 any individual resident outside India can buy listed Indian shares directly, without FPI registration, below 10% per company. Read more.

### Can OCI cardholders buy property in India?
Yes — residential and commercial, but not agricultural land, plantations or farmhouses. Read more.

### Do foreign clients deduct tax when paying Indian freelancers?
Generally no, if the foreign client has no Indian presence; the freelancer treats it as an export of services. Read more.

## For foreign companies: entering India

### Can a foreign company own 100% of an Indian company?
Yes in most sectors under the automatic route; some sectors and land-border-country investors need approval. Read more.

### Subsidiary, branch or liaison office?
Most choose a subsidiary (22% base tax option); a branch pays 35% plus surcharge; a liaison office can't earn income. Read more.

### Can we hire in India without an entity?
Yes, through an employer of record — but staff who conclude contracts can create permanent-establishment risk. Read more.

### What changed in Press Note 3 in 2026?
Investors with non-controlling beneficial ownership up to 10% from land-border countries can use the automatic route. Read more.

### Is the H-1B $100,000 fee being collected?
Not as of October 2026 — a court vacated it in June 2026 — but appeals and a 2026 extension proclamation leave it unsettled. Read more.

### What does a GCC in India cost in tax?
It's taxed on its cost-plus markup, usually at the 22% base option, with services to the parent zero-rated for GST. Read more.

## For foreign companies: tax and money

### Why is my Indian customer deducting 20%?
Indian law requires withholding on royalties and technical fees paid abroad; your treaty rate applies with a TRC, Form 41 and a no-PE declaration. Read more.

### What replaced Form 10F?
Form 41, under the Income-tax Rules, 2026. Read more.

### Does a foreign company need to file an Indian tax return?
Usually yes if it has Indian taxable income — unless its only income is dividends, interest, royalties or fees taxed at the full domestic rate. Read more.

### How are dividends to a foreign parent taxed?
20% plus surcharge and cess, or the treaty rate — 15% for a US parent with 10%+, 10% for UK, UAE, Japanese, German or Dutch parents. Read more.

### Does foreign SaaS need Indian GST?
Yes for sales to consumers and unregistered businesses — simplified registration, 18% IGST; B2B sales are reverse charge. Read more.

### Is India's equalisation levy still charged?
No — the 2% levy ended on 1 August 2024 and the 6% levy on online ads on 1 April 2025. Read more.

## Checking and buying Indian companies

### How do I verify an Indian company?
Check MCA master data, the GST taxpayer search and the IEC (all free), then read its filed accounts on MCA for about ₹100. Read more.

### Are private companies' accounts public in India?
Yes — financial statements and annual returns are filed with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and can be viewed for a small fee. Read more.

### What's the biggest due-diligence red flag in India?
Foreign investment that was never reported to RBI or was issued without a valuation — followed by GST mismatches and open tax demands. Read more.

### How is a share purchase from an Indian seller priced?
At or above fair value under FEMA, certified by a CA, merchant banker or cost accountant, with FC-TRS within 60 days. Read more.

## Trade deals

### Is the India–UK trade deal in force?
Yes — CETA took effect on 15 July 2026, with a 5-year social-security exemption for posted employees. Read more.

### Is the India–New Zealand FTA in force?
Yes — since 20 October 2026. Read more.

### Has India signed a trade deal with the EU?
Negotiations concluded on 27 January 2026; signature is pending, with entry into force expected later. Read more.

### Is the India–EFTA (Switzerland) agreement in force?
Yes, since 1 October 2025. Read more.
Latest changes: India FDI & foreign investment updates 2026.

Due diligence

# Transaction due diligence in India — for investors and acquirers abroad

Buying, investing in or partnering with an Indian company? We check the numbers, the tax position and the foreign-investment filings behind them — and tell you plainly what could hurt you after closing.

Discuss a deal
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Talk it through first — free. Book a 15-minute intro call with Durgesh to scope your requirement, timeline and fee.Book a free 15-min intro
Quick answers

- Financial due diligence in India tests a company’s quality of earnings, revenue and cash, working capital, debt and related parties — and, for foreign investors, whether past foreign investment was reported and priced under FEMA.

- Tax due diligence covers income-tax demands, TDS defaults, GST reconciliations and transfer pricing.

- Who does it: Chartered Accountants, usually alongside lawyers for legal diligence. We do it remotely and on the ground, reporting in English.

## Who it’s for

You are | Typical question | Usual scope | 

VC / PE fund investing in an Indian startup | Are the numbers real and are past share issues clean? | Financial + tax + FEMA + cap table | 

Foreign company acquiring an Indian business | What liabilities come with it, and what should the SPA cover? | Full financial, tax, FEMA, corporate and payroll | 

JV partner or distributor | Is this company what it says it is? | Company verification + financial review | 

Lender or procurement team | Can this supplier perform and pay? | Verification + filed financials + GST filing record | 

## What we check

- Financial: quality of earnings, revenue recognition, cash vs book profit, working capital, related-party transactions, debt and off-balance-sheet items, and how the Indian accounts map to your GAAP.

- Tax: income-tax assessments and open demands, TDS defaults, GST reconciliations (sales returns vs tax paid vs input credit), transfer pricing and pending litigation.

- FEMA / RBI: every past foreign investment reported (FC-GPR, FC-TRS), pricing-guideline compliance, ODI, ECB, the FLA return, sectoral caps and the beneficial-ownership position under Press Note 3.

- Corporate records: share-capital history, MCA filings, charges on assets, director KYC and board approvals — matched to the cap table.

- Payroll and labour: PF, ESI, gratuity and contractor arrangements.

- SPA input: findings turned into specific indemnities, conditions precedent and price adjustments for your lawyers. Checklist: due diligence checklist for Indian companies.

## Red flags we find most often in Indian targets

- Share allotments to foreign investors reported late — or not at all — and no valuation certificate on file.

- GST input credit claimed that suppliers never reported, and sales in the books that don’t match GST returns.

- Cash-heavy revenue or expenses routed through related parties.

- Income-tax demands sitting unanswered on the e-filing portal.

- Assets pledged to lenders (charges on MCA) that the management deck doesn’t mention.

- Key staff engaged as “consultants” to avoid PF and payroll tax.

## How it works

01
### Scope & NDA

## Frequently asked questions
Can you do due diligence on an Indian company without travelling to India?
Yes. Most of the work — data-room review, public records on MCA, GST and the income-tax portal, and management calls — is done remotely. We arrange site visits through our Indian offices where a deal needs them.

What does financial due diligence in India cover?
Typically quality of earnings, revenue and cash, working capital, debt and related-party transactions, plus tax exposures, GST reconciliations and — for foreign investors — whether past foreign investment was reported and priced correctly under FEMA.

Do you provide legal due diligence?
We cover financial, tax, FEMA and corporate-filing due diligence as Chartered Accountants. Legal opinions on contracts, title and litigation come from your lawyers; we coordinate with them so the reports fit together.

How long does due diligence on an Indian company take?
It depends on the size of the company and how quickly data arrives. We agree the timetable at the start and flag material issues as we find them rather than waiting for the final report.

Supplier checks

# Indian supplier verification — before you wire the advance

Importers, buyers and procurement teams abroad use us to check that an Indian supplier exists, is solvent and can actually make what it promises — through public records, its filed accounts and a visit to the premises.

Get a supplier checked
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Talk it through first — free. Book a 15-minute intro call with Durgesh to scope your requirement, timeline and fee.Book a free 15-min intro

## What we check

- Existence and status: MCA company master data, GST registration and return-filing record, import–export code.

- Financial strength: filed financial statements — revenue, profit, debt and charges on assets — compared with what the supplier told you.

- People: directors’ other companies, including struck-off ones, and who really owns the business.

- Bank details: that the account you’re asked to pay matches the legal entity.

- DIY version: how to verify an Indian company.

## The site visit

- Confirm the address, signage, operations and approximate scale.

- Photographs of the premises, machinery and stock (with the supplier’s permission).

- A short meeting with management on capacity, key customers and lead times.

- Visits are an observation report, not a technical quality inspection or a certification of goods.

## Where we cover

From our offices in Ahmedabad and Rajkot we cover Gujarat’s manufacturing belts — engineering, auto components, castings, ceramics, pharmaceuticals, chemicals and textiles — and from Mumbai and Bengaluru the western and southern hubs. Other locations are covered by arrangement.

## The report

A written report in English: what we checked, what we found, red flags and a plain-English conclusion. For bigger relationships — distribution, joint ventures, acquisitions — see due diligence in India.

## Frequently asked questions
How do I verify a supplier in India before paying?
Check the company's status on the MCA portal, its GSTIN on the GST portal and its import-export code, read its filed financial statements, confirm the bank account matches the legal entity — and for larger orders, have someone visit the premises.

Can you visit an Indian factory on our behalf?
Yes. We visit suppliers' premises, mainly in Gujarat, Mumbai and Bengaluru, and report what we see with photographs. It is an observation and records check, not a technical quality inspection.

What are the warning signs of a fake Indian supplier?
A struck-off or dormant company, a cancelled GSTIN, filed revenue far below what is claimed, bank details in another name, and pressure to pay an advance to a different entity.

Market entry

# India market entry research — decide with real numbers

Before you commit budget to India, get a feasibility study built by a CA: what the rules allow, what it will cost to set up and run, how it will be taxed — and who your competitors and partners really are, from their own filed accounts.

Plan your study
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Talk it through first — free. Book a 15-minute intro call with Durgesh to scope your requirement, timeline and fee.Book a free 15-min intro

## What’s in an India feasibility study

Question | What we answer | 

Can we do this in India? | FDI route (automatic or government approval), sectoral caps, licences and any land-border restrictions on your investors | 

Which structure? | Liaison office, branch, subsidiary, LLP, or an employer of record first — try the structure chooser | 

Where? | State, city, SEZ or GIFT City — incentives, talent cost and stamp duty differences | 

What will it cost? | Set-up, payroll (with PF, gratuity and statutory costs), rent, compliance and tax — year one and steady state | 

Who else is there? | Competitor and partner financials from public filings (below) | 

## Research from public filings — India’s hidden advantage

Every Indian company, private or listed, files its financial statements and annual return with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. That means you can see a private competitor’s revenue, margins, debt, shareholders and directors — something rarely possible in the US or UK. We pull and analyse these filings, plus GST registration and import–export codes, to size competitors, vet distributors and shortlist acquisition targets. How to run basic checks yourself: verifying an Indian company.

## Cost and tax model

- Subsidiary: can opt for a 22% base corporate rate (about 25.17% with surcharge and cess).

- Branch of a foreign company: taxed at 35% plus surcharge and cess.

- Money back to the parent: dividends, service fees and royalties each carry Indian withholding, reduced by your country’s treaty — see repatriating profits.

- GST: 18% on most services; exports of services can be zero-rated.

## What you get

- A go / no-go memo with the recommended structure and a 90-day entry plan.

- A three-year cost and tax model in Excel your finance team can adjust.

- A regulatory checklist with every registration and filing in year one.

- Competitor, partner or target profiles from public records.

- When you decide to go ahead, we can handle the company setup in India.

## How we work with clients abroad

- Fully remote: engagement letter and NDA by e-signature, data through your virtual data room or a shared drive, calls on your time zone (US mornings, Europe and Gulf afternoons, Japan and Singapore mornings IST).

- In English, in writing: every finding is referenced to a document or a public record, so your board, lawyers or auditors can rely on it.

- On the ground when needed: offices in Ahmedabad, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Rajkot and Dubai for site visits, bank meetings and management interviews.

- Clear scope: CA work — accounting, tax, FEMA and corporate filings. Legal opinions come from your lawyers; we work alongside them.

## Frequently asked questions
What is included in an India market entry study?
Regulatory mapping (FDI route, caps, licences), the recommended entity, a location view, a three-year cost and tax model, and competitor or partner research from public filings, ending in a go / no-go recommendation.

Can you get financial information on private Indian companies?
Yes. Indian private companies file their financial statements and annual returns with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, and these can be viewed for a small government fee. We analyse them for competitor and partner research.

Do foreign companies need government approval to enter India?
Most sectors allow 100% foreign investment under the automatic route with no prior approval. Some sectors, and investors with more than 10% beneficial ownership from countries sharing a land border with India, need government approval.

How is a foreign company's Indian subsidiary taxed?
As an Indian company. It can opt for a 22% base rate — about 25.17% including surcharge and cess — in exchange for giving up most deductions.

India entry

# Setting up in India? Subsidiary, LLP or branch — chosen and run properly

Foreign companies, overseas founders and India-focused funds use us to incorporate in India, report the foreign investment correctly and keep the Indian entity compliant from day one.

Plan your India entry
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Talk it through first — free. Book a 15-minute intro call with Durgesh to scope your requirement, timeline and fee.Book a free 15-min intro

## Your options for entering India

Structure | Best for | Key points | 

Private limited subsidiary | Most foreign companies: sales, engineering, GCCs | Foreign investment under the automatic route in most sectors; limited liability; can raise equity and issue ESOPs | 

LLP | Service businesses that want simpler governance | Foreign investment allowed only in sectors open to 100% FDI under the automatic route without performance conditions | 

Branch office | Foreign companies that need to operate as the same legal entity | Set up through an authorised dealer bank under RBI rules; taxed as a foreign company | 

Liaison office | Market research and representation only | No commercial activity or income in India | 

Project office | A specific contract in India | Limited to executing that project | 

RBI issued draft regulations in October 2025 to simplify how foreign companies open branch and liaison offices; until they are finalised, the existing regulations apply.

## Tax at a glance

- India’s Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026.

- An Indian subsidiary can opt for a 22% base rate (about 25.17% with surcharge and cess) in exchange for giving up most deductions.

- A branch of a foreign company is taxed at 35% plus surcharge and cess.

- Payments between the Indian entity and the parent — services, royalties, interest, dividends — follow India’s treaty with the parent’s country and transfer-pricing rules.

## Compliance from day one

- Resident director: every Indian company needs at least one director who stays in India for at least 182 days in the financial year.

- FC-GPR: report shares issued to the foreign parent on RBI’s FIRMS portal within 30 days of allotment. See the FC-GPR guide.

- FLA return: the annual foreign liabilities and assets return, due by 15 July.

- Transfer pricing: intercompany charges at arm’s length, an intercompany agreement and an annual accountant’s report — see transfer pricing.

- GST, TDS, payroll and ROC filings on a monthly and annual calendar.

## How we set you up

01
### Structure
Entity choice, sector check under the FDI policy, tax model and a resident-director plan.

02
### Incorporate
Name approval, incorporation, PAN/TAN, bank account, capital inflow and FC-GPR.

03
### Run
Books, payroll, GST, TDS, transfer pricing and monthly reporting to the parent — as your Virtual CFO.

## Setting up a GCC or offshore team

Many foreign companies set up an Indian subsidiary as a captive engineering, operations or finance centre, billing the parent on a cost-plus basis. That brings specific questions — the transfer-pricing markup, safe harbour, GST on exported services and hiring. Read setting up a GCC in India.

By country: USA · UK · UAE · Singapore.

## Frequently asked questions
How can a foreign company set up in India?
Most use a private limited subsidiary under the automatic FDI route. Alternatives are an LLP (only in sectors open to 100% automatic-route FDI without performance conditions), or a branch, liaison or project office set up through an authorised dealer bank under RBI rules.

Does an Indian subsidiary need an Indian director?
Yes. Every Indian company must have at least one director who stays in India for at least 182 days during the financial year.

What is the corporate tax rate for a foreign company's Indian subsidiary?
An Indian subsidiary is a domestic company. It can opt for a 22% base rate, about 25.17% including surcharge and cess, by giving up most deductions. A branch of a foreign company is taxed at 35% plus surcharge and cess.

What must be reported after the foreign parent invests?
Share allotments to the foreign parent must be reported in Form FC-GPR on RBI's FIRMS portal within 30 days, and the company must file the annual FLA return by 15 July.

Can you act as the finance team for our Indian entity?
Yes. After setup, Durgesh's team can run books, payroll, GST, TDS, transfer pricing and monthly reporting to the parent as a Virtual CFO engagement.

# Your Indian subsidiary, compliant and reported on time

Foreign parents use us as the finance team for their Indian subsidiary: books, payroll, GST, TDS, transfer pricing, FEMA and ROC filings — with a monthly pack in your format and one person accountable.

## The compliance calendar we run

When | What | 

Monthly | Bookkeeping and close, payroll, TDS deposit (7th), GST returns, PF / ESI (15th), withholding on payments to the parent (Forms 145 / 146) | 

Quarterly | TDS returns, advance tax, board meeting | 

Within 30 days of each share issue | FC-GPR on RBI’s FIRMS portal | 

15 July | FLA return to RBI | 

By 30 September | Statutory audit and AGM; director KYC | 

October–November | Transfer-pricing report, financial statements and annual return to MCA, income-tax return | 

Plus the resident-director requirement: at least one director who stays in India for 182 days or more in the financial year. Current dates for this season: compliance calendar October–November 2026.

## Transfer pricing

- Every charge between the subsidiary and the group — services, licences, loans, reimbursements, stock options — must be at arm’s length, documented and reported annually.

- Most captive service subsidiaries charge cost plus a markup; eligible IT and ITeS units can consider the safe-harbour option under the Income-tax Rules, 2026.

- We prepare the intercompany agreements, benchmarking and annual report, and keep the cost base clean month by month. More: transfer pricing guide.

## Reporting to the parent

- A monthly pack on your calendar: P&L, balance sheet, cash, headcount and budget vs actuals.

- Mapping from Ind AS / Indian GAAP to US GAAP or IFRS, intercompany reconciliations and audit support for the group auditor.

- Work in your group’s ERP or accounting system, with access controls you set.

## Paying the parent

Dividends, service fees, royalties and interest each carry Indian withholding tax, reduced by your country’s tax treaty with the right paperwork. From 1 April 2026, buybacks are taxed as capital gains in the shareholder’s hands. Full guide: repatriating profits from India.
